quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Ziad Al-Murshed): adjusted net income $33.4 billion, up 33% year-on-year and stable quarter-on-quarter; upstream adjusted EBIT $50.9 billion, up 14%, on realized prices of $108.1 per barrel (up 62%, with a record premium of more than $10 per barrel over Brent) despite lower production of 9.5 million barrels per day of oil equivalent (total liquids 7.6, per the CEO); downstream adjusted EBIT $6.2 billion, nearly twice a year earlier, and $11.7 billion for H1 (up 144%). ROACE 22.1%, gearing 6.2%; Q2 free cash flow excluding working capital $25.9 billion (up 42%); H1 operating cash flow $56.2 billion and H1 free cash flow excluding working capital $60.3 billion; cash of more than $60 billion at the end of Q2. The effective tax rate fell to 42.9% (45.1 in Q1) as refining and gas, taxed at 20%, contributed more profit.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted net income $33.4 billion (+33%); upstream adjusted EBIT $50.9 billion; downstream $6.2 billion; realized price $108.1 per barrel; production 9.5 million barrels per day

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO Ziad Al-Murshed): capital investments of $25.1 billion in H1 and 2026 guidance maintained at $50 billion-$55 billion, which excludes a potential investment in 'Humane' (as transcribed) under ongoing discussions. CEO Amin Nasser: the 2030 cash-flow growth targets remain achievable, driven mainly by gas production growth, downstream expansion and transformation; projects including Jafurah, Dammam and Zuluf remain on track.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex $50 billion-$55 billion; H1 capital investments $25.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Operations during the Strait of Hormuz disruption (CEO Amin Nasser): Aramco can restore production to pre-conflict levels within days and reach its maximum sustainable capacity of 12 million barrels per day within three weeks if asked; it uses the East-West Pipeline and West Coast refineries and terminals, can export around five million barrels via routes including the SUMED pipeline and Suez Canal, and is actively expanding export optionality. Loading capacity at its terminals rose 20% through faster vessel turnaround; more than 90% of materials for asset restoration in H1 were locally sourced, and its iktva program builds almost 70% of the supply chain within the Kingdom; restoration capability is six times faster than industry peers, per a third party.
quarterly_data.figure: maximum sustainable capacity 12 million barrels per day; around five million barrels exported via alternative routes; loading capacity +20%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Amin Nasser's market view: the U.S.-Iran conflict removed an average of 11 million barrels per day of liquid supply; the world lost over 2.6 billion barrels, about 1.8 billion net of bypass flows and reserve releases, with around 600 million barrels drawn from commercial inventories; Hormuz flows are a tenth of pre-conflict levels. He expects H2 demand around 2 million barrels per day above H1, replenishing inventories to require about 2.1 million barrels per day for up to 18 months on top of demand, governments to build additional strategic storage, and refining margins to stay exceptionally strong through H2 2026; rerouting via the Suez Canal and the Cape of Good Hope adds about 20 to 25 days.
quarterly_data.figure: 11 million barrels per day supply removed; 2.1 million barrels per day refill demand for up to 18 months
